nextjs-rendering-sr2-02.statement: The RSC Payload includes references to the JavaScript files for Client Components.
nextjs-rendering-sr2-02.explanation: Where a Client Component should render, the payload holds a placeholder and a reference to its JavaScript file, which the browser then uses to hydrate it.

nextjs-rendering-sr2-03.statement: On a direct visit, a Client Component can render on the server before browser hydration.
nextjs-rendering-sr2-03.explanation: Rendering on the server produces the first HTML, yet the component stays a Client Component: the same code also ships to the browser to hydrate that HTML.

nextjs-rendering-sr2-05.statement: React uses an incoming RSC Payload to reconcile the active component tree.
nextjs-rendering-sr2-05.explanation: The payload is a serialized description of the UI. When a new one arrives, React reconciles the component tree and updates the DOM to match.

nextjs-rendering-sr2-12.statement: Next.js can fetch a destination's RSC Payload before the user navigates to that route.
nextjs-rendering-sr2-12.explanation: Next.js prefetches routes linked with <Link> as they enter the viewport: a static route in full, while a dynamic route is skipped or only partly prefetched.

nextjs-rendering-sr3-01.statement: On an initial render, reading a pending Promise with use activates the nearest Suspense fallback.
nextjs-rendering-sr3-01.explanation: use suspends the component while the Promise is pending, so the closest Suspense boundary above it shows its fallback until the Promise resolves and the content replaces it.

nextjs-rendering-sr3-02.statement: Nested Suspense boundaries can reveal an outer section while deeper content is still loading.
nextjs-rendering-sr3-02.explanation: React streams the HTML of each boundary as it becomes ready, and later sends an inline script that swaps an inner fallback for its content once that content has loaded.

nextjs-rendering-sr3-03.statement: Components sharing one nearest Suspense boundary reveal together when their initial content is ready.
nextjs-rendering-sr3-03.explanation: By default the whole tree inside Suspense is one unit: if any part suspends, all of it shows the fallback, and then everything appears together.

nextjs-rendering-sr3-07.statement: A streamed HTML shell can include a Suspense fallback while that boundary's content is pending.
nextjs-rendering-sr3-07.explanation: The shell holds everything outside the Suspense boundaries, with each pending boundary's fallback in its place. React streams the content later with an inline script that swaps it in.

nextjs-rendering-sr4-08.statement: In the Pages Router, an automatically optimized page can receive query values in a post-hydration update.
nextjs-rendering-sr4-08.explanation: During prerendering the router's query object is empty, so on a dynamic route or a URL with query values, Next.js triggers another render after hydration to fill it in.

nextjs-rendering-sr5-01.statement: A Server Component can load its data by querying a database directly through a server-side database client.
nextjs-rendering-sr5-01.explanation: Server Components render on the server, so database credentials and query logic stay out of the client bundle.

nextjs-rendering-sr5-10.statement: SWR can use server-provided fallback data when its key matches the Client Component's useSWR key.
nextjs-rendering-sr5-10.explanation: The fallback only provides the hook's initial value. If the two keys drift apart, SWR ignores the fallback and fetches on the client.

nextjs-rendering-sr5-11.statement: A Client Component can read a data Promise passed from a Server Component through React's use API.
nextjs-rendering-sr5-11.explanation: Passing the Promise as a prop streams the data from server to client. Its resolved value must be serializable, and a Suspense boundary shows a fallback until it resolves.

nextjs-rendering-sr8-03.statement: A browser invokes a Server Action through an HTTP POST request when calling back to the Next.js server.
nextjs-rendering-sr8-03.explanation: Behind the scenes, actions use the POST method, and no other HTTP method can invoke them.
